info.title: INVENTRAK Inventory Management API
info.description: Backend API for the INVENTRAK inventory management system. Both the SQLite (Express) backend and the npm-free fallback expose this identical contract. Live docs: GET /api/docs

tags.name: Optimization
tags.description: EOQ, ROP, safety stock, ABC, turnover

post.summary: Promote a customer account to admin (admin only) â€” the public register endpoint hardcodes role 'customer', so this is the only way to create admins. Takes effect on the user's NEXT login (the token embeds the role at sign-in)

get.summary: Export a full database snapshot (admin only)
get.description: A copy of the entire durable database — every table it holds — as one JSON document. This is the record that survives a redeploy: the backend container filesystem is wiped on deploy, so an off-container snapshot is the only recovery path. Exported and restores are both audited. The snapshot contains password hashes: it is a backup, not a report, and it must be stored accordingly.

post.summary: Take a snapshot now and store it in the durable store (admin only)
post.description: The on-demand half of the scheduled backup: the same snapshot the timer takes (BACKUP_INTERVAL_MINUTES, default hourly), pushed immediately. Additive by construction — a push is a NEW row in the durable store, so it can never overwrite the copy an admin is relying on. Answers 503 with a reason when this server has no durable store to push to (SUPABASE_URL/SUPABASE_KEY or BACKUP_REMOTE_URL/BACKUP_REMOTE_KEY unset, store unreachable, or the snapshot is larger than BACKUP_MAX_BYTES).

503.description: No usable durable store: not configured, unreachable, or the snapshot exceeds BACKUP_MAX_BYTES. The body's error names the cause.

get.summary: Snapshots held by the durable store, newest first (admin only)
get.description: What a restore can start from, so recovery does not depend on a file that was downloaded before the container went away. Reports rather than throws: "the schedule is off" and "the store is unreachable" are states an operator needs to read (ok=false plus a reason), not errors to hide. Returns metadata only — the snapshot bodies are not shipped by a listing — and never the store key.

200.description: Scheduler configuration and the stored snapshots

post.summary: Restore the database from a snapshot (admin only)
post.description: Replaces the database contents with the supplied snapshot. Requires `confirm: true`, and the snapshot must come from the same driver this server runs. SQLite restores run inside a single transaction: a snapshot with dangling references is rejected and the live database is left untouched.

post.summary: Record a stocktake count (staff or admin)
post.description: What a person physically counted on a shelf, plus a snapshot of what the system believed at that moment. The snapshot is the only chance to capture it — once the stock column moves on, the variance the counter found can no longer be computed. Counting is a staff duty; reading the reconciliation is not (it reports money at risk).

post.summary: Record a shelf walk in one request (staff tier)
post.description: Records many counts at once for one shelf. The whole batch is validated before anything is written, then written in a single transaction: either every line in the walk is recorded, or none of them are — so a failure can never leave a shelf looking deliberately half-counted. A partial walk is still allowed and legitimate; it simply does not clear the shelf. A duplicate product_id within one batch is refused rather than silently resolved. Returns the shelf’s remaining work so the phone can update its progress without a second round-trip.

400.description: Validation failed; details list every offending line

get.summary: Shelf-vs-system reconciliation: shrinkage and unrecorded sales (admin only)
get.description: Compares the last physical count of each shelf against what the system believes and against the sales the till recorded since. unexplained = system_now - (counted - recorded_sales_since). Positive means the system believes stock that is not on the shelf; negative means more was found than expected. Reports units and money at risk; it deliberately does NOT assert a cause, because theft, breakage and a till error are indistinguishable from the data.

parameters.name: only_variance
parameters.description: Return only rows that are not balanced

get.summary: One shelf with every line on it, ready to be walked (staff tier)
get.description: Returns the shelf’s due status, its coverage, and per line what the system believes is there and when that line was last counted. Counts a shelf as re-counted only when EVERY line on it is inside stocktake_cycle_days, so the phone and the admin board can never disagree about whether a line is fresh. Computed on read.

get.summary: QR product lookup: resolve a scanned tag payload / SKU / bare id to a product (staff or admin)
get.description: The single round-trip behind QR product identification. Accepts the tag payload (INVENTRAK:PROD:<id>), a SKU (PRD-000042 or a custom code), or a bare numeric id (legacy barcode fallback). Returns the product, its QR tag data, a live per-location stock snapshot and open FIFO lots. The QR authorizes NOTHING â€” normal authentication, product status, location, quantity and approval rules all still apply after the scan.

parameters.description: Scanned QR content: tag payload, SKU or bare product id. URL-encoded when it contains colons.

post.summary: Record a counter / walk-in sale: decrements stock, consumes the FEFO lot, audits
post.description: The physical-store path. Writes the revenue row, decrements stock at the given location, consumes the expiring-first (FEFO) lot, refreshes the low-stock alert and writes a `sale.recorded` audit entry - all through the same helpers a staff stock-out uses, so the two cannot drift. Refuses with 409 rather than driving stock negative. Returns the consumption manifest so the till can show the customer which batch left.

lots_consumed.description: Which batches actually left the shelf, in FEFO order (soonest expiry first). Entries with lot_id null are units that sat on the shelf with no covering lot.

low_stock_alert.description: Set when the sale dropped the location to or below its critical level, so the till can say the reorder is due.

get.summary: Recount board: which shelves are due to be walked (admin only)
get.description: Returns one row per shelf with how far behind it is on its recount cycle. A shelf is re-counted only when EVERY product stocked on it has a count inside stocktake_cycle_days; a partial walk is reported as partial (coverage < 1) rather than resetting the shelf clock. Only products with stock on the shelf are counted — nothing stocked, nothing to walk. Empty shelves are never overdue. Computed on read, and the same pass raises and resolves stale_count flags on /api/alerts, so the board and the alert badge can never disagree.

customer_id.description: Links to the Customer Record this sale belongs to. Null on seeded/historical rows, which carry only a free-text name.

idToken.description: Google ID token from the OAuth sign-in flow

mfa_required.description: true when the admin has enrolled MFA and must complete the second factor

mfaToken.description: Short-lived (10 min) single-purpose challenge token for /api/auth/mfa/verify

secret.description: Base32 TOTP secret â€” paste into an authenticator app

otpauth_url.description: otpauth:// URI (QR) for Google Authenticator / Authy

code.description: 6-digit authenticator code OR a 12-char one-time recovery code (e.g. ABCD-EFGH-JKLM)
6-digit authenticator code proving possession of the secret
6-digit authenticator code proving possession of the secret

recovery_codes.description: One-time recovery codes â€” shown exactly once, stored only as hashes. Save them somewhere safe.
Fresh one-time recovery codes replacing the previous set (shown exactly once).

id.description: Product id (null only if the catalog row lacked one)

classification.description: F = Fast-moving, S = Slow-moving, N = Non-moving (no sales in the window)

transactions.description: Sales transactions for this product inside the window

frequencyDays.description: Average days between sales (null when non-moving)

recencyDays.description: Days since the last sale (null when non-moving)

ratePerDay.description: Average units sold per day over the window

valueSold.description: Revenue from in-window sales (qty x current price)

windowDays.description: Analysis window used (echoes the clamped query param)

payload.description: INVENTRAK:PROD:<id> â€” the exact string encoded in the printed tag; handy for reprinting.

locations.description: Quantity per storage-area name (Showroom, Stockroom 1, Stockroom 2).

status.description: Same bands as the Inventory page (total < 80 = low).

system_qty.description: What the system believed at the moment of the count

variance.description: counted_qty - system_qty: what the counter found

variance_at_count.description: counted - system at count time: the variance the counter found

count_undated.description: The count has no usable timestamp, so it cannot be reconciled against sales

expected_qty_now.description: counted - recorded sales since the count

unexplained_qty.description: system_qty_now - expected_qty_now. Positive = the system believes stock that is not there.

value_at_risk.description: unexplained units x SELLING price (cost is null across most of the catalog)

incomplete_sales_rows.description: Counts whose sales carry an unreadable timestamp

undated_counts.description: Counts that cannot be reconciled against sales at all

status.description: ok = every stocked line is inside the cycle. overdue = at least one line is past due, or some lines were never counted. never_counted = the shelf has stocked lines but no usable count at all. empty = nothing is stocked there, so there is nothing to walk.

total_lines.description: Products with stock on this shelf right now.

fresh_lines.description: Of those, how many have a count inside the cycle.

coverage.description: fresh_lines / total_lines. Stays below 1 until EVERY line is fresh — counting one line out of forty does not re-count the shelf.

due_at.description: When this shelf next needs a full walk. Anchored on the WORST line, never the newest: a fully-fresh shelf is due when its OLDEST fresh count ages out, a shelf with a stale line is already due, and a shelf with any never-counted line is due now (there is no date to count down from). A shelf that is not fully counted therefore never reports a future due date.

days_until_due.description: Negative once past due, by how many days the worst dated line is late. Zero when part of the shelf was never counted at all. Positive only when every stocked line is inside the cycle.

days_since_oldest_count.description: Age in days of the oldest count recorded on this shelf (null if none).

shelves_needing_count.description: Overdue or never counted — the shelves to walk today.

system_qty.description: What the system believes is on this shelf right now.

state.description: fresh = counted inside the cycle; stale = counted but too long ago; never = stocked here, never counted.

lines_remaining.description: How far the shelf still is from being re-counted.

ShelfStocktake.description: One shelf, in enough detail to walk it. Scoped to a single location on purpose: the whole-operation board (/api/stocktake) is admin-tier because it is an oversight view, while the person holding the phone only needs the shelf in front of them.

recorded.description: Lines written. Every line in the batch, or none.

shelf.description: The shelf's remaining work, so the phone updates without refetching.

submission_id.description: The admin-facing submission this correction targets (adjustment id or transfer id).

comment.description: What the approver wants the submitter to fix.

requested_by.description: Username of the admin who recorded the correction request.

status.description: Whether the submitter has addressed it.
Best-effort delivery status from the notification layer.

rate.description: How many to_unit equal one from_unit.

inquiry_id.description: Order inquiry this back order is attached to.

BackupSnapshot.description: A complete, self-describing snapshot of the database. Taken from one driver and restorable only on that same driver: the row shapes genuinely differ between SQLite and the store-backed backends, so a cross-driver restore is refused rather than silently corrupting data.

version.description: Envelope version. A snapshot is only restorable by a build that reads this version.

driver.description: Driver the snapshot was taken from. Restores are refused on a different driver.

generated_by.description: Username of the admin who exported the snapshot (null when unrecorded).

counts.description: Row count per table, so a snapshot can be inspected before it is trusted or restored.

tables.description: Table/dataset rows. Names are driver-defined. A store-level dataset that is one document rather than rows is carried as a single-row array.

confirm.description: Must be true. A restore deletes every row in every table before inserting, so an accidental or retried POST has to be refused.

snapshot_id.description: Restore a snapshot already held by the durable store instead of uploading one: "latest" for the newest, or an id from GET /api/admin/backups. Supply this OR snapshot, not both. This is the path that survives a wiped container, where the downloaded file is gone. The stored snapshot goes through the same envelope validation as an upload, so a foreign-driver snapshot is refused either way.

source.description: Where the restored snapshot came from — an uploaded body or the durable store. Recorded in the audit line too, because "which copy did we go back to?" is the first question after a recovery.

snapshot_id.description: Id of the durable-store snapshot that was restored, or null for an upload.

BackupSchedulerStatus.description: Whether the scheduled durable snapshot is live, where it goes, and how the last attempt went. Derived from the Supabase driver config when BACKUP_REMOTE_* is unset, so it reads enabled=true on any Supabase-backed deploy with no new env var. Reports the sink URL and table, never the key.

enabled.description: A durable store is configured (URL + key), so a snapshot can leave this container.

derived.description: True when the sink was derived from SUPABASE_URL rather than set explicitly via BACKUP_REMOTE_URL

keep.description: How many of the newest snapshots are retained in the durable store (BACKUP_KEEP)

interval_minutes.description: Timer period in minutes (BACKUP_INTERVAL_MINUTES); 0 means the schedule is off

max_bytes.description: Largest snapshot this deployment will push in one row (BACKUP_MAX_BYTES)

last_pushed_at.description: created_at of the last snapshot this process stored; null if this process has not stored one yet

last_error.description: Reason the last push failed, or null. A silent backup failure is how a deployment discovers it has no backups on the day it needs one.

pushed.description: Snapshots stored by this process since it started

created_at.description: When the snapshot was taken — the timestamp an admin chooses between

driver.description: Driver the snapshot was taken from; a restore is refused on a different driver

LastBackup.description: When the newest snapshot in the durable store was taken and whether that is getting old. Derived from the same listing this response carries, so the headline and the list can never disagree.

configured.description: Whether a durable store is configured at all. When false there is nothing to measure, so stale is null rather than false.

interval_minutes.description: The configured schedule period (0 = the timer is off)

stale_after_minutes.description: The age at which a snapshot counts as stale: twice the configured period, floored at twice the hourly default. Null only when there is no store to measure.

last_backup_at.description: created_at of the newest snapshot in the store (the one a restore would name). Null when the store holds none.

age_minutes.description: How long ago that snapshot was taken

stale.description: True when the newest snapshot is older than stale_after_minutes or the store holds none; null when it cannot be judged (no store, or an unreadable timestamp).

snapshot_id.description: Id of the newest snapshot (a restore can name it)

this_process_last_pushed_at.description: Last push made by THIS process (in-memory, so empty after a restart — the durable field above is the record)

last_attempt_error.description: Why the most recent push attempt in this process failed, if it did. A failed attempt never clears last_backup_at: the last GOOD backup is still what recovery would use.

reason.description: Why the verdict is what it is (no store, store unreachable, nothing pushed yet, unreadable timestamp)

ok.description: False when the durable store could not be read (see error), or when no store is configured at all

id.description: Id of the stored row, which is the snapshot_id a restore can name later

pruned.description: Older snapshots deleted by the retention window after this push

error.description: Why the durable store could not take the snapshot, naming the env vars that would fix it
